lines.text: Pearl dealers use a unit called momme.
lines.say: Pearl dealers use a unit called MOH-meh.

lines.text: One momme is a Japanese weight of exactly 3.75 grams.
lines.say: One MOH-meh is a Japanese weight of exactly three point seven five grams.

lines.text: A thousand momme make one kan, which is 3.75 kilograms.
lines.say: A thousand MOH-meh make one KAHN, which is three point seven five kilograms.

lines.text: Akoya pearl strands are priced by their total momme weight.
lines.say: ah-KOH-yah pearl strands are priced by their total MOH-meh weight.

lines.text: Wholesalers and producers use momme when they trade pearls.
lines.say: Wholesalers and producers use MOH-meh when they trade pearls.

lines.text: Pearl farms in Japan count their output in kan.
lines.say: Pearl farms in Japan count their output in KAHN.

lines.text: Silk uses momme too, but as a weight per area.
lines.say: Silk uses MOH-meh too, but as a weight per area.

lines.text: A round pearl's size is given as a diameter in millimeters.
Natural pearls are weighed in grains or carats.
Around 1893 Kokichi Mikimoto grew his first half round pearls in Japan.
lines.say: Around eighteen ninety three Kokichi MEE-kee-MOH-toh grew his first half round pearls in Japan.
